subject: zoology
question_text: What is exflagellation and what are the resultant products called?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.59, VSAQ 146). page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The process
lines: In the crop of the female Anopheles mosquito the
nucleus of the microgametocyte divides into
These nuclei pass into eight thin flagella-like
structures. The structures then lash about and
break away from the parent body.
This liberation of the flagella-like male
steps.why: The process is named for what is seen down the microscope — thin threads whipping off a body — so the answer describes the eight nuclei, the eight threads and the breaking away, in that order.
common_mistakes: Writing that exflagellation happens in man. It happens in the crop of the mosquito.
Giving the wrong number. Eight daughter nuclei give eight male gametes.
steps.memory_tip: Eight nuclei, eight lashing threads, eight gametes break free.
steps.margin_note: Three short lines in order: nuclei, threads, breaking away.

steps.label: The products
lines: The products of exflagellation are the male
One of them later enters the fertilization cone
steps.why: Naming the product also fixes the place of exflagellation in the cycle, because the very next event is fertilization inside the mosquito.
common_mistakes: Calling the products sporozoites. Sporozoites are formed much later, in the oocyst.
Calling them gametocytes. The gametocyte is what the gametes were formed FROM.
steps.memory_tip: Gametocyte to gametes: exflagellation makes the male gametes, not the sporozoites.
steps.margin_note: Name the product, then one line on what happens to it next.

insider_note: Half of this question is a counting mark — eight nuclei giving eight male gametes — so state the number plainly.
